text:
ConocoPhillips rose slightly today, but the stock has actually drifted lower over the past week—down about 3.6% from August 21. The main headwind appears to be oil prices themselves: US crude is trading at $83.90 per barrel, down from levels that would have supported higher energy stocks earlier this month. While geopolitical tension around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz might seem like it should push prices higher, the market is pricing in actual oil supply flows, not just risk—and those flows remain constrained by weak global demand signals.

The broader picture is that energy stocks are caught between two conflicting forces. Escalating US sanctions on Iran and its financial networks, plus renewed Navy enforcement in the Strait of Hormuz, do tighten global oil supply. But this week's news has been tilted toward diplomatic positioning (Iran calling for talks, Gulf nations resisting toll schemes) rather than a genuine supply crisis, so traders aren't rushing to bid up oil or refiners—yet.
